pairs.why: The two are nearly identical, but A's red saloon and slightly punchier contrast match the saturated, warm colour of the real cards better than B's greyer, flatter background.
This is the same pair swapped: B has the red saloon and livelier contrast closer to the real cards, while A's grey building reads duller.
B's hay bale is rendered as soft, smooth painted volume like the real cards, while A's stringy, strand-by-strand hay is the over-texturing the lessons reject.
A has the smoother painted hay that matches the real finish, while B's busy strand texture is too texture-heavy.
B's soft matte fabric suits read as cloth like the real cards' materials, while A's chrome-glossy suits look like a plastic statue, the too-glossy failure from the lessons.
This is the same pair swapped: A's matte cloth suits fit the real cards, while B's mirror-chrome suits are too glossy and look like toys.
B's lawn shows light blade texture and foreground leaves like the real backyard cards, while A's grass is close to ultra-smooth flat colour, which the lessons say is too far the other way.
This is the same pair swapped: A has the moderately textured grass and foreground leaves seen on the real cards, while B's lawn is almost flat.
